title: Interpretable machine learning finds a perpendicular-spin signature consistent with a spinon Fermi surface
summary: A correlator convolutional neural network trained on projective snapshots from numerical simulations of the Kitaev–Heisenberg model identified a characteristic correlation pattern in the intermediate gapless phase when analyzing spin snapshots perpendicular to the applied field. The authors interpret the learned pattern as Friedel oscillations of gapless spinons forming a Fermi surface, supporting earlier theoretical proposals for this phase and suggesting measurable correlations for future experiments.
ai_technology: Quantum-classical QuCl approach using a correlator convolutional neural network and regularization-path analysis
organization: Cornell University; The Ohio State University; Google Research; Harvard University; Ewha Womans University

evidence.tested: A correlator convolutional neural network trained on projective snapshots from numerical simulations of the Kitaev–Heisenberg model identified a characteristic correlation pattern in the intermediate gapless phase when analyzing spin snapshots perpendicular to the applied field.
evidence.unknown: This is a numerical/theoretical result based on DMRG wavefunctions and simulated snapshots, not an experimental observation of a quantum spin liquid. The authors interpret the learned motif as evidence consistent with a spinon Fermi surface and offer it as a prediction to guide experiments; they do not claim it is already experimentally confirmed.
evidence.ai_role: Analyzed simulated projective-measurement snapshots and surfaced the phase signature: spin correlations in the direction perpendicular to the magnetic field, interpreted as the spatial pattern of Friedel oscillations associated with gapless spinons.
